I am 68 years old and have farmed these 20 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. With only two of us at home and family working off-farm, I cannot waste labor or money on inputs that do not pay back. My wheat went into the ground last autumn, as it always does in the wheat-maize rotation. Now that the growing season has started, I will manage it with three well irrigations—reviving water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. I know this soil well, so I will top-dress nitrogen carefully; I have watched too many younger farmers lose their wheat to lodging because they poured on fertilizer greedily. I will apply moderate phosphorus and potassium because decades of rotation have kept the soil reasonably fertile. Two pesticide sprays on the wheat are enough for me—one for weeds and one if aphids or rust show up. When I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize using no-tillage direct seeding. At my age, trying to plough between wheat harvest and maize sowing is foolish; no-tillage saves my back, catches the season on time, and still gives a good crop. The maize will get two irrigations, timed at tasseling and grain filling, and two pesticide applications. I expect honest yields of about 520 kg per mu from wheat and 600 kg per mu from maize—steady returns that do not require me to gamble on expensive new tricks.
